slides.heading: Using for Loops for Totals
slides.body: Using for Loops for Totals is part of Definite Iteration. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Using for Loops for Totals
slides.body: A for loop can calculate totals by adding each value into an accumulator. This is common when working with scores and lists.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: Adding with a loop is like collecting coins one by one until the total is complete.

slides.heading: Example: Using for Loops for Totals
slides.code:
total = 0
for n in range(1, 4):
    total += n
print(total)

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Use for loops when you want to repeat through a known range or sequence.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Use a for loop to add numbers 1 through 5 and print total.
slides.hint: Loop over range(1, 6) and add each number to total.
